at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time to open the break on. Omit to roll now.

return_to.description: Source to rejoin afterwards. Omit to return to whatever is on air.

uri.description: File path or URI of the clip to roll.

AdStatus.description: An ad break, either armed for a future cue or currently on air.

on_air.description: False while it is prerolled and waiting for its cue.

return_to.description: Source to return to when the ad ends. None returns to the slate.

id.description: The name this filter answers to afterwards. A slug, and yours to pick.

params.description:
The filter's own settings. What goes in here is the filter's business,
not the core's.

programme.description: Filter the programme rather than one source.

side.description:
`input` puts it before the proxy boundary, where the thumbnail sees it
too; `programme` puts it on this source's programme branch only.

source.description:
The source to hang it on. Leave it out and set `programme` to filter
everything that goes out.

type.description: A filter type id, as `plugin.list` and `core.api` `kinds` report them.
A filter type id, as `plugin.list` reports them.

content.description:
What the item shows: `{"source": "cam1"}`, `{"ref": "<scene id>"}` or
`{"graphic": "plugin/id"}`.

draft.description:
A draft id from `scene.edit.begin`, to change a working copy instead of
the live document.

name.description:
What to call it. Left out, a source item is named after its source,
because a model reasons about words.

transform.description:
Where it goes. Left out, the next free cell of a grid over what is
already there, so a drop on a scene never needs a dialog.

AddOutputRequest.description:
`output.add`. The id and the URL are the whole of it for an RTMP
destination; anything else a kind understands rides in `params`.

policy.description:
Reconnect policy: "own" retries quickly, for servers you run; "cdn"
backs off harder, for platforms that penalise hammering.

uri.description: rtmp:// or rtmps:// URL including the stream key.

source.description:
Where the plugin comes from. One of: `owner/repo` (a GitHub release,
optionally `@version`), a git URL ending in `.git`, `cargo:name`,
`npm:@scope/name`, `pypi:name`, `oci:ref`, an absolute path to a
directory, or a bare plugin name to look up in the marketplaces.

color.description: A colour for every client, the tally and the Stream Deck to agree on.

id.description:
Stable id used by `program.take` and `source.remove`. Lowercase
letters, digits and dashes. Derived from the name or the host when
omitted, with a numeric suffix if that is taken.

kind.description:
"web" renders the URL as a page in the browser sidecar, the same as
writing `web+` in front of it. "auto" or omitted works the protocol out
from the URL.

name.description: Name shown to an operator. Defaults to the host of the URL.

superimpose.description:
Websites only: "auto" lets the mixer decode the page's own video
outside the browser and draw the page over the top, which saves about a
CPU core. "off" is the default.

uri.description: Stream URL, file path, or with kind "web" the address of a page.

black.description: Fraction of the picture at black. Default 0.98.

freeze_ms.description: How long the picture has to be identical. Default 200.

silence_ms.description: How long the programme has to be quiet. Default 500.

AgentExt.description: `ext.agent`. `true` takes the default thresholds; an object moves them.

Align.description: The nine alignment keywords, used to place content inside its frame.

frame.description: Answer with a still of the armed scene as well as the records.

item.description:
Which placement, by the name you gave the item or by its id. Left out,
every placement of this graphic is filled.

play.description: Bring it on after filling it in.

values.description: The fields, by name. `scene.item.schema` says which there are.

duration_ms.description: How long the change takes, in milliseconds. 0 is a cut.

scene.description:
The scene to apply it to. Left out, a new one is made. Applying onto an
existing scene keeps the item ids, so an animated layout change is a
property ramp rather than a cut.

values.description: The layout's parameters by name: its source slots and its numbers.

dry_run.description: Work out the plan and write nothing.

force.description: Take the preset's value wherever the operator already has one.

keep_sources.description: Leave the operator's sources and outputs alone.

name.description: A preset name, or a path to a directory holding `gmx-plugin.toml`.

applied.description: Present when the preset was actually applied.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written because `dry_run` was set.

live.description: The sources and outputs this core picked up without a restart.

needs_restart.description: What still needs a restart, in plain words. Empty is the good case.

plan.description: The whole plan, as JSON. The same object `preset.list` rows point at.

Asset.description: A file the collection carries with it.

path.description: Relative to the collection root, always.

Audio.description:
Whether the item's source is heard. A source is audible when any live item
of it says so, which is OBS's behaviour and changes no pad topology.

oneOf.description: Heard while the item is visible on programme.
Heard whether the item is visible or not.
Never heard.

AudioSetParams.description:
`source.audio.set` takes an id as well as the levels: the id comes off the
path on REST and out of the params on `/rpc`, and both land in one object.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for the whole source, 0.0 to 10.0. Omit to leave
it where it is.

media.description:
Gain per video underneath, by position. A null entry, or a list shorter
than the number of videos, leaves those alone: `[null, 0.0]` silences
the second video and touches nothing else.

muted.description:
Mute the whole source. Held apart from the fader, so unmuting comes
back to the level that was set.

page.description: Gain on a superimposed page's own sound.

param.description:
An expression over the collection's params and `W`, `H`. An empty
string takes the binding off.

prop.description: A geometry path such as `frame.w` or `position.x`.

Blend.description: OBS's blend enum, so an import carries across unchanged.

BridgeTransport.description: How media crosses between a node and the core.

oneOf.description:
RTP over UDP with RFC 6051 header extensions. The default: the receiver
knows the sender's timeline from the first packet.
SRT, for a link that loses packets. ARQ without inventing anything.
WHIP, for a WAN or a NAT nobody controls.

Bundle.description: What an importer is told before it reads the document.

assets.description: Every file carried, by the path inside the bundle.

id.description:
The collection's own stable id, repeated here so a listing can be read
without unpacking the document.

requires.description:
Every plugin this collection needs, with the version range that will
do. An importer that has none of them still gets the geometry.

skipped.description:
What could not be carried, one line each, so a partial export is
visible rather than silent.

written_by.description: The build that wrote it, for a bug report.

BundleAsset.description: One file carried in the bundle.

id.description: The asset id in the document.

path.description:
Relative to the bundle root, forward slashes. Never absolute: see the
head of this module.

Canvas.description:
The output raster. One per collection in this release; 11 section 1 leaves
room for several.

CanvasInfo.description: The canvas every source is scaled onto and every output leaves by.

source.description: None means this cell is the program return.

ConversionState.description: One conversion, in flight or remembered after it finished.

error.description:
Set only on `failed`, shown to the operator verbatim: "no AAC encoder
available" is worth more than "conversion failed".

progress.description: 0.0 to 1.0, position over duration, both read off the pipeline.

CoreInfo.description: `core.info`: what this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

features.description:
Feature strings a client can branch on: multiview, snapshot, uploads,
mcp, browser, exec-sources, rehearsal, tokens.

rehearsal.description:
True when the core was started with `--rehearsal`, which refuses
`output.add` and accepts rehearsal tokens.

token.description: Present when the request carried a token the core recognises.

ui.description:
What a surface should start with, when a preset chose it. Absent on a
core no preset has been applied to, which is what puts the welcome
panel up in the reference UI.

version.description: The build's own version, as in Cargo.toml.

layout.description:
A layout name from `scene.layout.list`. Left out, the number of sources
picks one.

sources.description: Source ids, in the order they should be laid out.

Crop.description:
How much of the content's own pixels to trim, normalised 0 to 1 so it
survives a canvas change. vMix and CasparCG do this; OBS crops in pixels,
which is why an OBS collection moved from 1080p to 720p loses its crops.

timeout_ms.description:
How long to look, shared between the devices. Two seconds by default,
four and a half at most, because no method blocks for five.

How long to listen. Capped at 4.5 seconds, so the call stays inside the
five second ceiling every method is held to.

draft.description: Pass this as `draft` on any `scene.item.*` call to edit the copy.

live.description: True when the client asked to edit on air.

scene.description: The scene it was taken from.

view.description: The scene as it stands, so the client has something to draw at once.

name.description: What to call the copy. A name already in use gets a number after it.
Name for the copy. The original's name and " copy" when omitted.

new_id.description:
Id for the copy. Derived from its name when omitted, with a numeric
suffix if that is taken.

live.description:
True to edit the scene that is on air as you go. The default is off
air: the draft is applied on the next take or on an explicit apply.

address.description:
Where the node is, for the record. The node always dials the core, so
this is what `node.list` shows before it has.

name.description:
What the node will call itself. A slug: it goes in `place` and in the
node's certificate.

ttl_secs.description: How long the token is good for. Default one hour.

format.description:
`json` for the document alone, `zip` for a bundle with its assets, or
`dir` for the same bundle unpacked.

path.description:
Where to write it, on the machine the mixer is running on. Required for
`dir`. For `zip`, leaving it out hands the bytes back as base64.

Ext.description:
The `ext` table from 03 section 6.

Every key is off by default. A terminal UI takes meters and tally and
declines multiview; a Stream Deck takes tally only; an agent takes nothing.

agent.description:
`event/agent.state` when a threshold crosses or a state flips, with a
snapshot URL. `true` takes the defaults from 09 section 5 item 12.

multiview.description:
The mosaic: binary frames and `event/multiview.layout`. `false` or
omitted builds nothing.

preview.description:
The preview scene, composited in the multiview pipeline at mosaic size,
or `"full"` for a full resolution preview compositor built while
subscribed. See 11 section 3.

telemetry.description:
`event/telemetry`: a line of numbers per tick, at 1 to 10 per second.
This is what turns the probes on; nothing measures until it is here.

Filter.description: One filter in an item's chain.

type.description: The plugin qualified provide id, for example `chroma/filter`.

FilterIdRequest.description: `filter.remove`, and anything else that names one filter.

FilterRecord.description: One filter as the core reports it.

FilterReport.description: A source filter that had to be copied onto each placement.

placements.description: The items it was copied onto, by their path in the document.

code.description: A stable machine readable code, so a client can filter or translate.

detail.description: The numbers behind the message, for a client that draws them.

items.description: The items involved, in the order the message names them.

message.description: One sentence naming the state and the next step.

scene.description: The scene it is in, when it is about one.

Fit.description:
How content fills its frame. SVG's vocabulary, which replaces OBS's seven
bounds types and maps onto `sizing-policy` on a `glvideomixer` pad.

oneOf.description: The content's own size, scaled by `scale`. The frame is ignored.
Fit inside the frame, keeping the aspect ratio.
Fill the frame, keeping the aspect ratio, cropping the overflow.
Fill the frame exactly, distorting the aspect ratio.
Scale so the width matches; the height falls where it falls.
Scale so the height matches; the width falls where it falls.
Like `contain`, but never scale up past the content's own size.

FlatContent.description:
Content on the wire. The same four shapes as the tree, except that a group
names no children: they are records whose parent is the group.

Flush.description: `event/flush`: the end of a batch. A client renders here and not before.

seq.description: The sequence number of the last event in the batch.

Found.description: One thing found on the network.

name.description: The instance name, which is the node's name.

Frame.description: The rectangle an item is fitted into.

opacity.description: The item's own opacity multiplied by every group's above it.

path.description:
The names from the top item down, so a message can say
`corner / pulpit` rather than an id.

source.description: Present for an item whose content is a source.

source_width.description:
The canvas, which is what the document knows about a source's own size
until the mixer says otherwise. Named so a client that does know can
tell the two apart.

GoLiveRequest.description: `program.golive`: add the page, add the destination, take the page.

id.description: Source id. Derived from the host when omitted.

rtmp.description:
Where to send the programme. Added as an output unless one already
sends there. Omit to leave the outputs alone.

url.description: The page to put on air. Plain http(s); `web+` is added here.

output.description: The output that was created or reused, if one was asked for.

source.description: The source that was created or reused.

state.description: Where the source is now. It goes to programme as soon as it is live.

GraphicType.description: One graphic this core can place, as the catalogue has it.

designer.description:
The `[provides.designer]` block, when the plugin wrote one: the icon
for the add gallery, the UI schema, the default frame and the gizmos.

manifest.description: The OGraf manifest's path inside the plugin, so a client can fetch it.

type_id.description:
The plugin qualified id an item's `content.graphic` names,
`ograf/lower-third`.

name.description:
The tray folder to put them in. Null takes them out of the one they
are in.

Header.description:
Everything in the document that is not a scene or an item: the name, the
canvas, the collection's parameters, the transitions it carries, the assets
and the source labels.

It is not a record and it has no id, so it cannot be diffed the way the
tree is. It is carried whole, because it is small and because the
alternative is that a command touching only the header produces an empty
patch and is thrown away by `edit`, which is exactly what used to happen to
`scene.params.set`, `source.set` and `source.group`: all three answered with
the change and none of them kept it.

HeaderChange.description: The header as it was and as it is.

limit.description: How many takes to return, newest first. At most 100.

undo.description: How many steps are still on each stack, so a UI greys out a button.

Id.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. Minted ids are version 7 (time ordered); ids derived from a layout are version 8.

path.description:
The collection JSON exported from OBS (Scene Collection, Export), as a
path on the machine the core is running on.

config_toml.description:
The `[[sources]]` block to paste into a config, so the sources the
scenes draw can be added in one edit rather than one call each.

filters_duplicated.description:
OBS attaches a filter to a source, so a camera keyed in one scene is
keyed in all of them. Here filters belong to the item, so a source
filter is copied onto each placement and each copy is named here. This
is the one thing an import changes the meaning of, so it is reported
rather than left for somebody to find on air.

scenes.description: The scenes that were added, by the names they ended up with.

skipped.description: What could not be brought across, and why, one line each.

source_report.description:
Every OBS source and what became of it: carried across, needing a
plugin that is not installed, or skipped with the reason.

sources.description: The sources the collection needs, which have to be added separately.

path.description:
The bundle: a `.zip` or the directory it unpacks to, as a path on the
machine the core is running on.

bundle.description: What the bundle said about itself.

missing_plugins.description:
Plugins the collection needs that this core has not got. The scenes
still came across; those items will draw nothing until it does.

relink.description:
Assets that did not come across, with the items that draw them. Empty
when everything landed.

scenes.description: The scenes that were added, by the names they ended up with.

InstanceRecord.description: One running instance and its cost.

plugin.description:
The plugin it belongs to. Carried on the instance as well as on the
plugin, because `plugin.stats` is a flat list and a caller holding one
row should not have to go back for the name.

enabled.description: Turn a filter off without taking it out.

filter.description: The filter's name, or its position in the item's chain from 0.

ItemProps.description:
An item's props, which is an `Item` with the children lifted out into their
own records.

item.description: The item's name or its id.

type.description:
The item type: a graphic id like `ograf/lower-third`, or a plugin
provide like `camera/source`.

edge.description: `align`: left, right, top, bottom, center-x, center-y.

seq.description:
A client's own sequence number, echoed on the patch. See
`SetItemRequest::seq`.

Layout.description: A scene's geometry, for copying onto another one.

scene.description: The scene it came from, for a message.

match.description:
`name` matches item names first and falls back to slot order; `order`
uses slot order alone.

description.description:
What the layout calls its own scene, which is the nearest thing it has
to a description.

params.description: The whole JSON Schema, so a client renders an inspector from it.

sources.description:
The parameters that take a source id, in the order sources are poured
into them.

LayoutItem.description:
One item's geometry: everything about where it sits and nothing about what
it shows.

Limits.description:
The ceilings a client should plan against rather than discover by being
refused.

event_queue.description: How many events the bus holds before a slow client is told to resync.

max_call_secs.description:
Longest any method blocks before it answers. The tightest client
default in the wild, so nothing here can time out a client that used
its own.

max_gain.description:
Loudest a fader can be asked for. Out of range is clamped to this
rather than refused.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest upload the media endpoint accepts, in bytes.

duration_secs.description:
How long before it goes back down. A minute by default, which is long
enough to reproduce a fault and short enough that a forgotten firehose
stops on its own.

categories.description:
The categories actually raised, which is what the caller asked for
with anything GStreamer does not know dropped.

LogSetRequest.description: `log.set`. Name an instance or a target, not both.

instance.description:
A plugin instance: a source or an output id. Its lines carry the id,
so raising this one raises only that camera.

level.description:
`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`, or `default` to stop
overriding this one.

target.description:
A module path prefix such as `godwinmix::mixer`. The longest match
wins, so a more specific override still beats a broader one.

label.description:
What to call the group of changes that follows. Omit it to end the
group, so the next change is its own undo step.

conversion.description:
Where a conversion of this file stands, None when none was asked for in
this process's lifetime.

duration_ms.description:
None when the file could not be inspected; it is still listed, because
an operator would rather see a clip they cannot read the length of than
wonder why it is missing.

faststart.description:
The converted copy's absolute path when one exists on disk. This is
what "add as source" should prefer over `path`.
Whether the moov atom comes first (a player can start before the whole
file arrives). None for a non-ISO container, never a reason to convert
on its own. See `convert::moov_first`.

name.description: Name shown in the UI, relative to the library root.

path.description: Absolute path, which is what gets handed back to the ad break API.

reasons.description: Why it is not, in words an operator can act on. Empty when it is.

video_codec.description:
Short codec name of the first video stream ("h264", "vp9"), None when
there is no video or it could not be inspected.

web_safe.description:
True when the file needs no conversion to play in a browser: H.264 plus
AAC (or no audio) in an MP4. See `convert::web_safety`.

error.description:
Set when the directory itself could not be read, so the UI can say why
the list is empty instead of just showing nothing.

Meters.description:
`event/meters`: the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10
per second, rather than one message per meter as the legacy stream sends.

program.description: Peak dBFS per channel on the programme bus.

sources.description: Peak dBFS per channel, per source id.

ad.description: Present while an ad break is armed or running.

program.description:
Source currently on program, or None while the slate is showing. A
scene of one full canvas item reports that item's source here too, so
anything written against this before scenes existed still reads.

running_time_ms.description:
Program pipeline running time. Cues are scheduled against this, not
against wall clock, so a client can place a break on a known frame.

scene.description: The scene on air, when one was taken by name.

to_scene.description: The scene it is going to.

fps.description: Frames per second, 1 to 30. The core clamps to what the mosaic runs at.

MultiviewExt.description: `ext.multiview`. Accepts `false` to mean off, or an object.

MultiviewLayout.description: `event/multiview.layout`: how to read the binary frames that follow.

id.description:
Stable for as long as the cells are unchanged, and carried in the
header of every frame, so a client that falls behind can tell which
layout a late frame belongs to.

cells.description:
Cell index to source id, in reading order. Cell 0 is the program return
when it is enabled.

fps.description: Frame rate of the mosaic, so the UI can size its own expectations.

NameRequest.description: `media.convert` and `media.remove` name a file rather than an id.

name.description:
File name as it appears in the media listing. The REST layer puts it
in the path, where the transform rule calls it `id`, so both spellings
are read.

listening.description: Whether this core is listening for nodes at all.

id.description: The node's name, as it was enrolled.

NodeView.description:
What `node.get` reports about one node, and what `node.list` reports about
all of them.

heartbeat_age_ms.description:
Milliseconds since the last heartbeat. The same number
`gmx_node_heartbeat_age_ms` carries.

instances.description: The instances it is hosting right now.

plugins.description: The plugins this node has, name and version.

provides.description: The provide ids this node can run, `<plugin>/<provide>`.

state.description:
`online`, `offline`, or `expected` for a node listed in the config that
has never dialled in.

Ograf.description:
The OGraf manifest, in the subset this host reads.

Everything else the file carries is kept in `rest` and passed on: OGraf is
an EBU specification that will grow, and a key this build has not heard of
is a key a newer client may want. Dropping it here would make the core the
thing that has to be upgraded first.

id.description: The graphic's own id, as the OGraf file gives it.

main.description: The module the web component is in, relative to the manifest.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema of the graphic's own data. What the inspector renders
and what `scene.apply_graphic` fills by name.

stepCount.description: How many steps `playAction` walks through. One means in and out.

has_key.description:
False while the address still carries a placeholder a preset wrote in
for somebody to replace, such as `YOUR-STREAM-KEY`. The key itself
never leaves the core, so this is how a client knows to put its own
form up and say "needs a stream key" without ever seeing the key.

True for an address with no key in it at all, an SRT one for instance,
because there is nothing there for anybody to replace.

queue_secs.description:
Seconds of encoded data waiting in the pre-muxer queue. A number that
climbs and stays high means the destination cannot keep up.

Override.description: A sparse change to one item of a referenced scene.

client_seq.description:
The client's own sequence number, echoed back.

A drag cannot wait for a round trip, so the client kit draws the move
itself and reconciles when the echo arrives. Without this it cannot
tell an echo of the move it has already drawn past from a correction,
and the handle rubber bands backwards under the cursor. Every geometry
command carries a `seq`; this is that number coming back.

header.description:
The collection's own properties, when they changed. Absent for the
ordinary case, which is every command that moves an item.

label.description: What the client called this change, for a label in an undo menu.

scope.description:
`document` today. `presence` (who is looking at what) is the other
scope 11 section 4 names and is not implemented.

seq.description:
Monotonic, per core. A client that sees a gap asks for a fresh
snapshot rather than guessing.

source_client.description:
Whoever asked for the change, so a client can suppress the echo of its
own edits and not fight its own optimistic drawing.

PipelineDot.description:
What `pipeline.dot` answers with on `/rpc`. The REST route serves the same
graph as `text/vnd.graphviz`, so `gmx dot | dot -Tsvg` needs no unwrapping.

dot.description: The graph itself, in the dot language.

PipelineRequest.description:
Which pipeline to look at. A source id, an output id, `programme` or
`multiview`. `pipeline.list` says what is running.

Place.description: Where an instance runs: core, in-process, sidecar, or node:<name>.

PluginDescription.description: The whole of one plugin, for an agent about to use it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

manifest.description: The manifest as JSON, every table of it.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

schemas.description: Per provide id, its settings schema.

skills.description: Per provide id, the description line from its SKILL.md.

source.description: Where it was installed from, as it was typed.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

trust.description:
What was checked about where this came from: "signed", "signed, digest
only", or "custom, unreviewed". 06 section 4: an operator can only
judge a plugin if the catalogue says what was checked.

plugins_dir.description: Where plugins are read from on this machine.

PluginName.description:
Anything that names one plugin.

The field is `id` because that is what the REST layer fills in from
`/api/v1/plugins/{id}`, and a plugin's id is its name: the namespace of
every id it contributes. `name` is accepted as well, for a JSON-RPC caller
who wrote the obvious thing.

PluginRecord.description: One plugin as the core reports it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

source.description: Where it was installed from, as it was typed.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

trust.description:
What was checked about where this came from: "signed", "signed, digest
only", or "custom, unreviewed". 06 section 4: an operator can only
judge a plugin if the catalogue says what was checked.

provides.description: What went with it, so a caller can see the blast radius.

schemas.description: The JSON Schema every surface renders, one per provide.

handshake_ms.description: How long the new build took to answer `initialize`.

anyOf.description:
`"full"`: a full resolution preview compositor, built while subscribed
and torn down after.

Thumbnails at mosaic size, which is what a designer drawing handles
wants and costs about 1.7 percent of a programme composite.

draft.description:
A draft from `scene.edit.begin` for the preview to draw in place of
the armed scene, which is how a designer sees what it is laying out.
What is armed is left as it is, and `scene` is ignored. An empty string
goes back to the armed scene; so does applying or discarding the draft.

scene.description: The scene to arm. Null or omitted disarms.

path.description:
The Unix socket to connect to, absolute. Read it with `unixfdsrc` in
GStreamer, or with the media contract's own reader.

transport.description:
What is on the far end, so a client knows what to expect before it
connects.

ProgramState.description:
What `program.get` answers with, and what `program.take` returns so that no
follow up read is needed.

ad.description: Present while an ad break is armed or on air.

preview.description: The scene armed for the next `program.take` with no argument.

previous.description: The previous source, which is what `program.revert` would take back to.

program.description:
Source on air, or null for the slate. A scene of one full canvas item
reports that item's source here too, so anything written against this
before scenes existed still reads.

running_time_ms.description: Programme pipeline running time, in milliseconds.

scene.description: The scene on air, when one was taken by name.

order.description: A fractional key. Siblings sort by it; see `order.rs`.

parent.description:
The scene this item is in, or the group item it is a child of. Absent
for a scene, which hangs off the document itself.

Relink.description: One asset an import could not put back.

items.description:
The items that draw it, by scene and item name, so the person fixing
it knows what will be blank until they do.

path.description: The path the document asks for.

reason.description: Why it could not be used: missing, or a hash that does not match.

after.description: Put it in front of this one. With neither, it goes to the front.

seq.description: A client's own sequence number, echoed on the patch.

provides.description:
The provide ids used, `ograf/lower-third`, so a reader can see what the
collection actually asks the plugin for.

versions.description:
A semver range, `^0.2.0`, or `*` when the exporter had no version to
name because the plugin was not installed where the export ran.

Resync.description: `event/resync`: the client fell behind and the stream has a hole in it.

from_seq.description:
The last sequence number the client is known to have. Everything after
it was dropped; re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot.

name.description: The new preset's name. A slug: lower case letters, digits and hyphens.

out.description: Where to write it. Defaults to `~/.godwinmix/presets/<name>`.

scene.description: The scene's name or its id.

armed.description: True for the armed scene, which is the preview.

items.description: How many items, groups counted with their children.

sources.description:
Every source the scene draws, so a picker can grey out one whose
sources are missing without reading the whole document.

SceneView.description: One scene as a command answers with it.

findings.description:
What `scene.validate` would say about it, so a client shows a warning
without asking again.

geometry.description:
Where each item actually lands, after groups are flattened and
references resolved. Bottom of the stack first, which is the order the
compositor takes them in.

records.description: The scene's own record and one per item, parents before children.

term.description:
A word to look for in a plugin's name, description or kind. Empty
lists everything.

installed.description: Whether it is already on this mixer.

tier.description: custom, bronze, silver or gold. 06 section 4.

version.description: The newest listed version this core's api range can run.

position_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the start of the clip. Off either end is clamped
rather than refused, so a scrubber flicked past the end lands there.

secs.description: How far back to read, in seconds. An hour by default, a day at most.

params.description: The settings to apply. Only the keys named are changed.

SetItemRequest.description: `scene.item.set`: a state assignment. Only the keys named move.

duration_ms.description: How long to take getting there, in milliseconds. 0 is a cut.

easing.description: `linear` or `ease`. Only meaningful with a duration.

props.description:
Any of `name`, `transform`, `crop`, `opacity`, `blend`, `visible`,
`locked`, `audio`, `content`. A key left out is left alone.

seq.description:
A client's own sequence number, echoed on the patch so a drag can
discard the echoes of moves it has already drawn past.

SetOutputRequest.description:
`output.set`. Change one destination in place, naming only what moves.

The id picks the output and is never changed by this; renaming one is a
remove and an add, because the id is what alerts, hooks and the runtime
store call it.

queue_secs.description: Seconds of encoded data to hold before the muxer.

uri.description:
The whole new address, stream key and all. Write only: no method ever
reads it back, so leaving it out keeps the address already in force
and a client can offer "change the buffer" without holding the key.

settings.description: Only the keys named are changed.

SetSourceRequest.description:
`source.set`: a full state assignment for one source.

Every field is optional and only what is named moves, which is how every
other setter in this protocol works. The one that matters here is `place`:
it moves a running source between the core, a sidecar and a node.

Unknown fields are refused rather than dropped. Serde's default is to
ignore what it does not recognise, and a setter that answers 200 to a field
it threw away is indistinguishable from one that saved it: the first party
drawer sent `uri` here for months and told the operator it was saved.

color.description:
The colour the UI and the tally show it in. On the scene document,
like the name.

id.description:
Source id. `source` is accepted too, which is what the scene side of
this method has always been called with.

latency_ms.description: The latency budget in milliseconds, answered on the LATENCY query.

name.description:
What to call it in the UI. Kept on the scene document, so every
client, the tally and an agent read the same name.

params.description: Params for the source's own kind. Merged over what it has.

transport.description: How a remote source's media travels: `rtp`, `srt` or `whip`.

Severity.description: How much the reader should care.

oneOf.description: The scene will not composite as written.
It will composite, and it is probably not what was meant.
Worth knowing before going to air.

Loud enough to page someone. Nothing raises it yet; it is here so the
severity ladder in `protocol.json` is the one 03 section 6 names.

Snapshot.description: `event/snapshot`: the full state, and where in the stream it sits.

SnapshotRequest.description: `snapshot.get` on `/rpc` and through MCP. The REST route serves the same bytes raw, because an `` tag cannot read base64 out of JSON.

allow_large.description: Permit a width above the `[snapshot] max_width` ceiling.

force.description: Ignore the per client rate limit for this one request.

id.description: "sheet", "program", or a source id. A `.jpg` on the end is accepted.

width.description:
Scale down to this many pixels across, keeping the aspect. Never
enlarges. Omit for the `[snapshot] default_width` of 320, which is
enough to see who is in shot; `width: 0` for the cell's own size.

SourceAudioState.description:
What a source's audio controls read back as, which is what the audio
endpoint answers with.

Wider than `SourceAudio` because the fader and the mute apply to every
source, while the page and media balance belongs only to a superimposed one.
Every number here is read off the elements after the request landed, so a
request whose gain was clamped answers with the gain that took effect.

page.description:
Absent on anything but a superimposed source, which is the only kind
with separate sounds to balance.

SourceMeta.description: A source's name, colour and tray folder, as this collection has them.

color.description:
Free text so a client can use whatever it draws with. Absent means the
client picks one by kind.

group.description:
A tray folder: a tag on the source, purely for finding things. Not a
scene group, which is a thing on the canvas.

SourcePositionState.description:
Where a seekable source has got to, which is what the seek endpoint answers
with.

Both numbers are read back off the pipeline after the seek has landed, not
taken from the request. A seek snaps to a key unit, so the frame an operator
asked for and the frame they got are rarely the same millisecond, and a
scrubber drawn from the request would sit a little away from the picture.

duration_ms.description: Absent while the demuxer has not worked the duration out yet.

SourceReport.description: One line of the report: an OBS source and what happened to it.

oneOf.description: It came across whole.
It came across, and the plugin that plays it is not installed yet.

It did not come across. `placeholder` names what was put in the scene
in its place, when anything was.

obs_type.description: The OBS plugin type, for example `ffmpeg_source`.

placements.description: How many items in the collection use it.

oneOf.description: Pipeline is up but no media has arrived yet.
Buffers arriving within the stall timeout.

Was live, then went quiet. Its program pad is held at alpha 0 so the
slate shows through rather than a frozen frame.
The input pipeline errored. A retry is scheduled.

audio_idle_ms.description:
Same for audio. `None` here while `has_audio` is true means the source
advertised an audio track that never produced a decoded sample.

cell.description: Index into the multiview grid, or None while the source has no cell.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for this source, 0.0 silent through 1.0 unity to a
ceiling of 10.0. Read back off the volume element rather than remembered,
so what the UI shows is what the pipeline is doing.

muted.description:
Muted by the operator. Held apart from the fader so that unmuting returns
the source to where it was rather than to unity.

position_ms.description:
Where this source has got to, and how long it runs, in milliseconds.
`None` on anything not seekable, and on a seekable source whose duration
the demuxer has not worked out yet.

seekable.description:
True when this source can be scrubbed. A file can be. A camera, an RTMP
feed or a page cannot, and asking one to is a mistake worth refusing
rather than quietly doing nothing.

video_idle_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last video buffer, or None if none has arrived.

SubscribeRequest.description: `core.subscribe`: which events, and which expensive streams.

events.description:
Event name patterns, matched against the part after `event/`. `*`
matches one or more characters: "program.*" matches `event/program.took`.
An empty list subscribes to everything.

ext.description:
The expensive streams this client wants. Nothing here runs unless a
client asks for it.

SubscribeResult.description: What `core.subscribe` answers with, before the snapshot arrives.

events.description: The event patterns now in force.

ignored_ext.description: `ext` keys this build ignored. Empty on a build that knows them all.

seq.description: The sequence number the snapshot that follows is current as of.

at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time the cut landed on.

by.description: Token id that asked for it, or "core" when the mixer did it itself.

seq.description: Event sequence number the take was published under.

source.description: What went on air. Null is the slate.

at_running_time_ms.description:
Programme running time to land the cut on, in milliseconds. Omit for
immediate. Read the current running time from `core.info` or a status
snapshot first.

scene.description:
The scene to take, by name or by id. `source` wins when both are
given; with neither, the armed scene goes on air.

source.description: Id of the source to put on air.

transition.description: "fade", or {type, duration_ms, params}. Absent is a cut.

task_id.description:
The id a long running method answered with. Spelled `id` on the REST
route, where it is in the path, and `task_id` everywhere else, which
is what 03 section 6 calls it.

age_secs.description: Seconds since the task was started.

kind.description:
The method that started it, so a client reading a list knows what it is
looking at.

poll_interval_ms.description: How long to wait before asking again, while it is still running.

progress.description: 0 to 1 where the work can say, absent where it cannot.

result.description: The body the method would have answered with, once it is done.

hz.description: Ticks per second, 1 to 10. The core clamps to that range.

TelemetryExt.description:
`ext.telemetry`. Accepts `false` to mean off, `true` for the default rate,
or an object naming it.

TokenInfo.description:
What the calling token is allowed to do, echoed back so a surface can grey
out what it cannot reach instead of discovering it at the first refusal.

confirm.description: "none" or "required": whether destructive calls need a confirm token.

profile.description: MCP tool profile this token is meant for: "standard" or "minimal".

arguments.description: The tool's own arguments, as its input schema describes them.

name.description: `<plugin>/<tool>`, or the bare tool name when only one plugin has it.

Transform.description: Where an item sits and how it is sized.

anchor.description:
Normalised 0 to 1 within the item's own box: (0,0) top left, (0.5,0.5)
centre, (1,1) bottom right.

frame.description:
The rectangle the content is fitted into, in canvas pixels. Absent
means the content's own size, scaled.

position.description: Canvas pixels, of the item's anchor point.

Transition2.description: A named transition between two scenes.

TransitionRequest.description: How a take gets there. See docs/reference/transitions.md.

duration_ms.description: How long it takes. 0 is a cut.

params.description: A stinger takes clip, cut_at_ms, luma.

type.description: cut, fade, move, stinger, or a plugin name.

UiDefaults.description:
What a surface starts with: the layout, the theme and the gallery mode.

Chosen by a preset (`preset.apply`), carried in `core.info` and pushed as
`event/ui.changed`. None of it changes what the core does. It exists so the
first page a volunteer sees is the one their preset chose rather than the
one the last person to use this browser chose. 05 section 3b is where the
four gallery modes are defined.

gallery.description:
`live`, `snapshot`, `icon` or `label`. Absent means the surface asks
the machine, which is what `gmx doctor` proposes.

layout.description: Slot to panels, top to bottom. Empty means the surface's own default.

preset.description: The preset that set these, so a surface knows one has been applied.

theme.description: A theme id the surface resolves, for example `dark` or `calm`.

Update.description: One record as it was and as it is.

source.description:
Where the new build comes from. Defaults to wherever this plugin was
installed from last time.

scene.description: Leave it out to check the whole collection.

ok.description: True when there is nothing to fix.

Vec2.description: A point or a pair of factors.

description: The GodwinMix control protocol. One set of methods, events and types, whether the peer is a UI on /rpc, curl on /api/v1, the CLI, the MCP server or a plugin on stdio.

envelope.description: Keys accepted on every method, handled before a method runs.

confirm.description: The confirm_token from a -32020 refusal, valid 30 seconds. Only a token whose policy is confirm = required needs it.

dry_run.description: On any destructive method. Answers the diff it would make and would_change, against the live state, and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: On any mutating method. The answer is kept for 24 hours; a replay returns it with replayed: true. The same key with different params is -32602 with data.idempotency = mismatch.

trace_id.description: Carried into the answer, the X-Trace-Id header and the log line. Taken from the W3C traceparent header over HTTP, or generated.

errors.meaning: the envelope was not a JSON-RPC request
the params were wrong for this method
the core failed while handling the call
not in a state that allows this
the plugin did not declare that placement
the plugin died during the call
a protocol line was over 4 MiB
the change needs the instance restarted
a confirm token is needed first

events.name: event/snapshot
events.summary: The full state, and the sequence number it is current as of. Sent on subscribe and after any change the deltas cannot describe.

events.name: event/program.took
events.summary: The programme changed. Carries the running time the cut landed on, so a client can see how close a scheduled take was to its mark.

events.name: event/scene.patch

client_seq.description: The client's own sequence number, from the `seq` on the command, so a drag discards echoes of moves it has already drawn past.

source_client.description: Who asked for the change, so a client suppresses the echo of its own edits.

events.summary: One change to the scene document, as records rather than a snapshot: what was added, what changed with its before and after, and what was removed. One per transaction, batched and ended by event/flush.

events.name: event/preview.changed
events.summary: A scene was armed, or the arming was cleared. The armed scene is the preview, and program.take with no argument takes it.

events.name: event/source.state
events.summary: A source moved between connecting, live, stalled and failed.

events.name: event/source.position
events.summary: How far through a seekable source has got, a few times a second. Never sent for a camera, which has no position to report.

events.name: event/output.state
events.summary: A destination connected, dropped or is retrying.

events.name: event/adbreak.changed
events.summary: An ad break was armed, went on air, or ended.

events.name: event/ui.changed
events.summary: The surface defaults changed: a preset was applied, or an operator set the layout, theme or gallery mode by hand. Nothing on air moves.

events.name: event/hook.blocked

hook.description: The hook name, for example take.before.

plugin.description: The plugin that owns it, or the URL or command when it came from [[hooks]] in the config.

reason.description: What went wrong and what to do about it.

events.summary: A hook did not get its say: it did not answer inside its timeout, or the thing behind it could not be reached. Whatever the hook was attached to went ahead anyway, which is the rule that keeps a slow hook off the frame path. See 03 section 8.

events.name: event/media.changed
events.summary: A file in the library was uploaded, deleted, or its conversion moved on.

events.name: event/meters
events.summary: Peak dBFS for the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10 per second. Replaces the two separate meter events on /ws.

events.name: event/tally
events.summary: Which sources are on programme, on preview, or off. Derived by the core so a Stream Deck does not have to.

events.name: event/alert
events.summary: Something an operator should see. Also written to the log and to the alert webhook.

events.name: event/telemetry

black.description: fraction of the picture at or below black, 0 to 1

lufs_s.description: short term loudness over three seconds, approximated from the programme meter

shot.description: how much the picture changed since the last frame, 0 to 1

sources.description: source id to 1 when it is live and 0 otherwise

events.summary: Numbers instead of a picture, up to ten times a second and under 200 bytes: the shot change score, the black ratio, a freeze flag, short term and integrated loudness, a silence flag and which sources are live. From cheap probes on the raw programme frames, which run only while a client is subscribed.

events.name: event/agent.state

payload.description: The concise agent.state document, plus `why` (one of program, black, freeze, silence, shot) and `snapshot`.

events.summary: The agent.state document, pushed when a telemetry threshold crosses or a take lands, with `why` naming which and a snapshot URL beside it. Edge triggered and at most one a second, so a picture that stays black is one message rather than one a tick.

events.name: event/multiview.layout
events.summary: How to read the binary frames that follow: the cells, and the layout id carried in every frame header.

events.name: event/multiview.frame

payload.description: 16 byte header then JPEG. Not a JSON message.

events.summary: A mosaic frame, as a binary WebSocket frame rather than JSON: a 16 byte little endian header (seq u32, layout id u32, programme running time in milliseconds u64) then the JPEG. The top bit of seq is the stream and is clear on a mosaic frame; the other 31 bits count.

events.name: event/preview.frame

payload.description: 16 byte header then JPEG. Not a JSON message.

events.summary: The armed scene as a picture, on the same socket and in the same 16 byte header as a mosaic frame, with the top bit of seq set to say so and the layout id zero because there is no grid to cut up. One picture per frame: draw it whole.

events.name: event/resync
events.summary: This client fell behind and events were dropped. Re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot; nothing between from_seq and the new snapshot arrives.

events.name: event/flush
events.summary: The end of a batch. Render here and not before, so a client never paints half an update.

ext.turns_on: the mosaic pipeline, built on the first subscriber and stopped on the last, plus event/multiview.layout and the binary frames
per source thumbnails from a node

event/preview.frame: the armed scene, composited in the multiview pipeline from the per source thumbnails and published on this socket, to /mjpeg/preview, to scene.preview.frame and to its own cell on the mosaic. "full" composites it at the canvas's own size while a client is subscribed, so a designer's handles land on real coordinates

filter.description: A green, blue or custom colour key

output.description: FLV over RTMP or RTMPS, the ingest every CDN takes
MPEG-TS over SRT, in caller or listener mode
Record the encoded programme to a new MP4 or Matroska file

source.description: An RTMP or RTMPS publisher, decoded with the hardware the machine has
A continuous stream: HLS, DASH, RTSP, SRT, RTP or UDP
A finite clip on disk or over HTTP, scrubbable, ending with EOS
A command whose process writes a container to stdout
A web page rendered as a live source, by the sidecar or by wpesrc
A web page drawn over the video it was playing, decoded here rather than in the browser
A test pattern and a tone, for the conformance harness

methods.name: adbreak.end
methods.summary: Cut a running ad short, or disarm one that is scheduled.

methods.name: adbreak.start
methods.summary: Interrupt the programme with a clip, then rejoin live when it ends.

methods.name: agent.state
methods.summary: The compact document written for agents: the programme, each source's state and a motion score saying how much its picture is changing.

methods.name: codec.list
methods.summary: Every codec and element in the catalogue, which of them this machine actually has, and what it would pick.

methods.name: core.api
methods.summary: Every method, event and type as JSON Schema. The same document as protocol.json and `godwinmix --api-info`.

methods.name: core.doctor
methods.summary: The environment checks: GStreamer, the elements, the config, the disk and the ports. The same list `gmx doctor` prints.

methods.name: core.info
methods.summary: What this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

methods.name: core.session_log
methods.summary: The append only record of everything that happened, back as far as you ask.

methods.name: core.shutdown
methods.summary: Stop the mixer, and with it the programme. Nothing else takes the show off air, so this is deliberately its own call.

methods.name: core.startup_report
methods.summary: How long each stage of the start took, and what was over the 250 ms mark.

methods.name: core.status
methods.summary: The full state: programme, every source, every output, the multiview grid, the encoder backend and any ad break.

methods.name: core.subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribe to the event stream. WebSocket only: the core answers event/snapshot then deltas, ending every batch with event/flush.

methods.name: device.discover
methods.summary: Ask every device plugin what it can see: cameras, NDI senders, publishers. Each candidate's params are ready for source.add.

methods.name: filter.add
methods.summary: Hang a filter on one source or on the programme, live.

methods.name: filter.list
methods.summary: Every filter in place, with what it is and where it sits.

methods.name: filter.remove
methods.summary: Take a filter out of the pipeline.

methods.name: filter.set
methods.summary: Change a filter's settings in place. A filter that cannot take the change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: log.gst
methods.summary: Raise GStreamer's own debug categories for a while, then let them fall back on their own.

methods.name: log.levels
methods.summary: Every log level override in force, and the GStreamer categories still raised.

methods.name: log.set
methods.summary: Change one instance's or one module's log level while the mixer runs.

methods.name: media.convert
methods.summary: Transcode a library file to a web safe copy, in the background.

methods.name: media.list
methods.summary: The clips in the library, with durations and whether each has audio.

methods.name: media.remove
methods.summary: Delete a library file and its converted copy. Refused while it is a live source.

methods.name: media.upload
methods.summary: Stream a file into the library. HTTP only: the body is the file.

methods.name: node.discover
methods.summary: Look for nodes on the local network over mDNS. A network without multicast finds nothing and the [nodes] table in the config is the way there.

methods.name: node.enrol
methods.summary: Mint a one time enrolment token for a node. The answer carries the command to run on the other machine. The token is good for one enrolment and expires.

methods.name: node.get
methods.summary: One node: its clock offset, how long since its last heartbeat, the plugins it has, and the instances it is hosting.

methods.name: node.list
methods.summary: Every node this core knows about: the ones connected now, the ones that have gone quiet, and the ones the config expects that have never dialled in.

methods.name: node.remove
methods.summary: Forget a node. Its bridge is closed, every token minted for a plugin on it is revoked, and its certificate stops working. Sources placed on it go to the slate until they are moved or the node enrols again.

methods.name: output.add
methods.summary: Send the programme to another destination. The encoder is shared, so adding one costs nothing on air.

methods.name: output.get
methods.summary: One destination.

methods.name: output.list
methods.summary: Every destination, with its state, reconnect count and how much is buffered.

methods.name: output.reconnect
methods.summary: Drop and re-establish one destination's connection now, without waiting for its reconnect policy.

methods.name: output.remove
methods.summary: Stop sending to a destination and forget it. Other outputs are unaffected.

methods.name: output.set
methods.summary: Change a destination in place: a new address with a new stream key, a new reconnect policy, a deeper outage buffer. The address is write only, so a client that only wants the buffer never has to hold the key.

methods.name: pipeline.clock
methods.summary: The clock every pipeline is running against, and how far each one has got.

methods.name: pipeline.dot
methods.summary: One pipeline as a graphviz graph: every element, every pad and the caps negotiated between them.

methods.name: pipeline.latency
methods.summary: How much delay one pipeline is carrying, and which stage put it there.

methods.name: pipeline.list
methods.summary: Every pipeline running right now, by the name the other pipeline methods accept.

methods.name: pipeline.queues
methods.summary: Every queue in one pipeline with how full it is, fullest first. A queue that stays full is where the trouble is.

methods.name: plugin.add
methods.summary: Install a plugin, while live, from any source form: a GitHub release (owner/repo), a git URL, cargo:, npm:, pypi:, a local directory, or a bare name looked up in the marketplaces this mixer knows. The signature and the api level are checked before anything is copied.

methods.name: plugin.describe
methods.summary: One plugin in full: its manifest, the settings schema of every provide, and the description from each SKILL.md.

methods.name: plugin.disable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin off without uninstalling it. It registers nothing and runs no process until it is enabled again.

methods.name: plugin.enable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin back on. It registers what it declares and its instances start.

methods.name: plugin.list
methods.summary: Every plugin installed, with what it provides and what each running instance is costing in cpu, memory, latency, dropped buffers and restarts.

methods.name: plugin.reload
methods.summary: Read a plugin's directory again and swap its running instances one at a time, with the freeze frame covering each.

methods.name: plugin.remove
methods.summary: Uninstall a plugin and unwind everything it registered: its provides, its tools, its panels, its hooks and its discovery matchers.

methods.name: plugin.search
methods.summary: Search every marketplace this mixer knows for a plugin, by name, description or kind. Answers what `gmx plugin add <name>` would install.

methods.name: plugin.settings.get
methods.summary: A plugin's settings as they stand, with its schema beside them.

methods.name: plugin.settings.set
methods.summary: Change a plugin's settings. A plugin that cannot take a change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: plugin.stats
methods.summary: Per instance cpu, memory, media latency, dropped buffers and restarts, refreshed once a second.

methods.name: plugin.update
methods.summary: Fetch a newer build of a plugin, install it beside the one that is running, and prove it starts. A build that does not answer `initialize` within ten seconds is rolled back and the plugin that was working stays working.

methods.name: preset.apply
methods.summary: Put a preset on this core: its config, its scenes, its layout, its theme and its gallery mode. Pass dry_run to get the plan and write nothing.

methods.name: preset.list
methods.summary: Every preset this core can apply: the six built in, plus anything installed beside the binary or under ~/.godwinmix/presets.

methods.name: preset.save
methods.summary: Turn this core's working setup into a preset directory somebody else can apply. Stream keys and the control token are replaced with placeholders.

methods.name: preview.close
methods.summary: Give up a raw frame socket. The socket goes when the last holder closes it.

methods.name: preview.open
methods.summary: Open a raw frame socket on this machine for a source or the programme, and answer with its path. No encode anywhere: a client on the same host reads the frames the mixer already has. Close it with preview.close.

methods.name: program.get
methods.summary: What is on air, the programme running time, and what revert would go back to.

methods.name: program.golive
methods.summary: One call to put a web page on air: add the page, add the destination, and take the page as soon as it renders.

methods.name: program.history
methods.summary: The last hundred takes, newest first, with the token that asked for each.

methods.name: program.revert
methods.summary: Take back to the shot before this one.

methods.name: program.take
methods.summary: Put a scene or a source on programme. The cut is instant and the outgoing stream is not disturbed.

methods.name: scene.add
methods.summary: Make an empty scene, or one built from a set of sources.

methods.name: scene.apply_graphic
methods.summary: Fill a graphic that is on a scene, by field name, and optionally play it on or take it off. Answers with the records and, if asked, a still.

methods.name: scene.apply_layout
methods.summary: Apply a layout, making a scene or reshaping one that exists. Applying onto an existing scene keeps the item ids, so the change is a ramp and not a cut.

methods.name: scene.create_from
methods.summary: A scene from a set of sources, laid out by the built in layout for that count (full, two-box, three-box, quad, then a grid) or by a named one.

methods.name: scene.duplicate
methods.summary: A copy of a scene with new ids throughout, so editing the copy cannot touch the original.

methods.name: scene.edit.apply
methods.summary: Write a draft back into the live document.

methods.name: scene.edit.begin
methods.summary: Take a working copy of a scene. Editing is off air by default: the draft is written back on the next take of that scene, or when you apply it.

methods.name: scene.edit.discard
methods.summary: Throw a draft away. The live document is untouched.

methods.name: scene.export
methods.summary: The whole collection: as JSON, or as a zip bundle carrying its assets with a hash each, which is what you send somebody.

methods.name: scene.get
methods.summary: One scene: its records and where every item actually lands on the canvas.

methods.name: scene.graphic.list
methods.summary: Every graphic template this core can place, with what each one takes.

methods.name: scene.history.mark
methods.summary: Group the changes that follow into one undo step, until the next mark. This is what makes a drag of forty moves one Ctrl+Z.

methods.name: scene.import
methods.summary: Read a collection bundle, a zip or the directory it unpacks to, and add its scenes to this one. Answers with a relink report for any asset that did not come across.

methods.name: scene.import.obs
methods.summary: Read an OBS Studio scene collection and add its scenes to this one.

methods.name: scene.item.add
methods.summary: Put something on a scene's canvas. With no transform it lands in the next free cell, so a drop never needs a dialog.

methods.name: scene.item.align
methods.summary: Line items up on an edge: left, right, top, bottom, center-x or center-y.

methods.name: scene.item.arrange_grid
methods.summary: Lay items out in a grid of `cols` columns.

methods.name: scene.item.bind
methods.summary: Bind a geometry property to an expression over the collection's parameters, so changing a number moves everything that follows it.

methods.name: scene.item.copy
methods.summary: Copy an item into another scene. The copy keeps the transform and the filters and gets a new id.

methods.name: scene.item.cover_canvas
methods.summary: Put items over the whole canvas, filling it and letting the overflow go.

methods.name: scene.item.distribute
methods.summary: Space items evenly between the two on the ends, horizontally or vertically.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.add
methods.summary: Hang a filter on one item, so a camera keyed in one scene is not keyed in all of them.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.remove
methods.summary: Take a filter off an item.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.set
methods.summary: Change one of an item's filters, or turn it off without taking it out.

methods.name: scene.item.fit_to_canvas
methods.summary: Put items over the whole canvas, keeping their aspect ratio inside it.

methods.name: scene.item.group
methods.summary: Put items into a group. The picture does not change.

methods.name: scene.item.match_size
methods.summary: Make items the same size as another one.

methods.name: scene.item.move
methods.summary: Move an item to another scene, keeping its transform and filters.

methods.name: scene.item.remove
methods.summary: Take an item off a scene.

methods.name: scene.item.reorder
methods.summary: Move an item up or down the stack, between two named neighbours.

methods.name: scene.item.schema
methods.summary: What one item type takes: a graphic's OGraf schema, or a source or filter plugin's settings schema. The same JSON Schema every client renders an inspector from.

methods.name: scene.item.set
methods.summary: Assign an item's properties. Only the keys named move; the rest are left alone, so calling it twice with the same body changes nothing the second time.

methods.name: scene.item.ungroup
methods.summary: Take a group apart, leaving every child exactly where it looked.

methods.name: scene.layout.copy
methods.summary: Read one scene's geometry, to paste onto another.

methods.name: scene.layout.list
methods.summary: The layouts that ship with the core, with the parameters each one takes.

methods.name: scene.layout.paste
methods.summary: Put one scene's geometry onto another's items, matched by name first and slot order second. Items that match nothing are left alone.

methods.name: scene.list
methods.summary: Every scene in the collection, with how many items it has, the sources it draws and whether it is armed.

methods.name: scene.params.get
methods.summary: The collection's typed parameters, readable without their values, so a client discovers what is fillable before filling it.

methods.name: scene.params.set
methods.summary: Set the collection's parameter values, declaring any that are new. A `{{name}}` in any string property of any item follows them, so one call changes every lower third that uses it.

methods.name: scene.preview.frame
methods.summary: A still of the armed scene as base64 JPEG, the floor every client has.

methods.name: scene.preview.set
methods.summary: Arm a scene. The armed scene is the preview, and program.take with no argument takes it.

methods.name: scene.redo
methods.summary: Put back what undo took away.

methods.name: scene.remove
methods.summary: Delete a scene. What is on air is not touched.

methods.name: scene.rename
methods.summary: Change a scene's name, its colour, or both. Names and colours live on the document, so every client, the tally and an agent see the same ones.

methods.name: scene.transaction.abort
methods.summary: Throw the batch away. The document goes back to where it was when the batch opened.

methods.name: scene.transaction.begin
methods.summary: Start a batch. Everything until the commit applies on one frame or not at all, and undoes in one step.

methods.name: scene.transaction.commit
methods.summary: Apply the batch.

methods.name: scene.undo
methods.summary: Undo the last change. A drag marked with scene.history.mark undoes as one step.

methods.name: scene.validate
methods.summary: Overlaps, items off the canvas, safe area breaches and missing sources: what to fix before saying a scene is done.

methods.name: snapshot.get
methods.summary: One JPEG: the whole contact sheet, the programme, or one source cut out of the mosaic.

methods.name: source.add
methods.summary: Add a source while the mixer runs. Answers with the id it got and the whole source record.

methods.name: source.audio.set
methods.summary: Move a source's audio: the fader, the mute, and for a superimposed page the balance between its own sound and the videos under it.

methods.name: source.duplicate
methods.summary: Add another source like one the mixer has: the same address and settings under a new id. A client cannot do this with source.add, because the address it is shown has everything after the host cut off.

methods.name: source.get
methods.summary: One source. Refused with the ids that exist when there is no such source.

methods.name: source.group
methods.summary: Put sources in a tray folder. A tag for finding things, not a group on the canvas.

methods.name: source.list
methods.summary: Every source, with its state, whether it has video and audio, and its fader.

methods.name: source.remove
methods.summary: Remove a source. If it is on programme the mixer cuts to the slate first.

methods.name: source.restore
methods.summary: Put back a source that source.remove took away, as it was: same id, address, settings, fader and mute. The mixer remembers the last sixteen it removed, until it restarts.

methods.name: source.seek
methods.summary: Move a seekable source to a position. Answers with where it actually landed.

methods.name: source.set
methods.summary: Change a running source: its name and colour, its params, or where it runs. The name and colour live on the scene document. Moving a source between the core, a sidecar and a node is `place`; the programme keeps its frame rate across the move and the compositor covers the swap.

methods.name: task.cancel
methods.summary: Ask a piece of long running work to stop. Cooperative: the answer says the request landed, not that the work has stopped yet.

methods.name: task.get
methods.summary: How a piece of long running work is getting on, and its answer once it has one.

methods.name: task.list
methods.summary: Every background job this core knows about, newest first.

methods.name: tool.call
methods.summary: Call one of a plugin's tools, in MCP's shape. The name is `<plugin>/<tool>`, or the bare tool name when only one plugin has it.

transports.framing: one JSON-RPC message per text frame; mosaic frames are binary

godwinmix mcp, a thin adapter over these same methods

well_known.note: the reference web UI, served from the binary
the JSON-RPC WebSocket. Everything in `methods` is reachable here.
